stages.say: Build a hash map from scratch. No built-in dictionary.

stages.title: It has to grow
stages.say: A million keys go in. What happens to your chains? Make it stay fast.
stages.require: Add `Capacity`; the map resizes so `Count <= Capacity * 0.75`. A million puts and gets in under 2 seconds.

stages.title: Many threads
stages.say: Now many threads read and write it. Make it safe without one global lock.
stages.require: Add `StripedIntHashMap` with `Put`, `Get`, `Remove`, `AddOrIncrement(key, by)`, `Count` — safe under concurrency, per-key exact.

prompts.label: Check my design — no code
prompts.text: I believe an array of buckets with separate chaining, a bit-mixing index so patterned keys spread out, doubling at load factor 0.75 for amortised O(1) puts, and lock striping for concurrency. Review my reasoning without giving me the implementation. What would break it?

prompts.label: Review, do not rewrite
prompts.text: Review my implementation for correctness and edge cases. Do not rewrite the code. List problems most severe first, each with the input that triggers it.

prompts.label: Race conditions
prompts.text: Now review this implementation for race conditions if multiple threads call Put concurrently. For each race, give the interleaving that breaks it. Then name the smallest synchronization boundary that preserves correctness. Do not write code yet.

prompts.label: Tests that expose bugs
prompts.text: Suggest tests that could expose bugs in my implementation: boundaries, duplicates, empty and invalid input, and concurrency where it applies. For each, say why the expected value is correct.

prompts.label: Complexity check
prompts.text: What is the time and space complexity of each public method as written? Do not claim a bound unless every step achieves it.

prompts.label: Requirement change
prompts.text: The requirement changed: Add Capacity; the map resizes so Count <= Capacity * 0.75. A million puts and gets in under 2 seconds. List which members need to change and which do not, before writing any code.

learn.title: 1 · Problem
learn.md: Implement an integer hash map **without using any built-in dictionary**: `Put(key, value)` inserts or updates, `Get(key)` returns the value or `-1`, `Remove(key)` deletes it, and `Count` is the number of keys.

learn.title: 2 · Clarifications
learn.md:
- Can I use Dictionary or HashSet inside? (No.)
- Get on a missing key? (−1, as LeetCode.)
- Expected size — do I need to resize? (Stage 2.)

learn.title: 3 · Key insight
learn.md: A hash map is an array plus a rule for collisions. Chaining keeps that rule simple; what makes it fast is keeping chains short — a good hash spreads keys, and resizing keeps the load factor bounded.

learn.title: 4 · Approach
learn.md: I would say, before coding: "A."n array of buckets with separate chaining, a bit-mixing index so patterned keys spread out, doubling at load factor 0.75 for amortised O(1) puts, and lock striping for concurrency."

learn.title: 11 · AI usage strategy
learn.md:
- Make the design decision yourself, then ask the assistant to attack it.
- Delegate the mechanical parts only after the structure is fixed.

**Prompts for this question:**

- *Check my design — no code* — "I believe an array of buckets with separate chaining, a bit-mixing index so patterned keys spread out, doubling at load factor 0.75 for amortised O(1) puts, and lock striping for concurrency. Review my reasoning without giving me the implementation. What would break it?"
- *Review, do not rewrite* — "Review my implementation for correctness and edge cases. Do not rewrite the code. List problems most severe first, each with the input that triggers it."
- *Race conditions* — "Now review this implementation for race conditions if multiple threads call Put concurrently. For each race, give the interleaving that breaks it. Then name the smallest synchronization boundary that preserves correctness. Do not write code yet."
- *Tests that expose bugs* — "Suggest tests that could expose bugs in my implementation: boundaries, duplicates, empty and invalid input, and concurrency where it applies. For each, say why the expected value is correct."
- *Complexity check* — "What is the time and space complexity of each public method as written? Do not claim a bound unless every step achieves it."
- *Requirement change* — "The requirement changed: Add Capacity; the map resizes so Count <= Capacity * 0.75. A million puts and gets in under 2 seconds. List which members need to change and which do not, before writing any code."

learn.title: 12 · Common AI mistakes
learn.md:
- key % size with a power-of-two size: keys that are multiples of the size all collide.
- Negative keys giving a negative index.
- Never resizing — every chain grows linearly.
- Rehashing by re-inserting through Put (counts twice, may resize recursively).
